title: 2010 AMC 12B 21
statement: Let \(a\gt0,\) and let \(P(x)\) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \[ \begin{aligned} &P(1)=P(3)=P(5) \\ &\quad {}=P(7)=a, \end{aligned} \] and \[ \begin{aligned} &P(2)=P(4)=P(6) \\ &\quad {}=P(8)=-a. \end{aligned} \] What is the smallest possible value of \(a?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(1, 3, 5, 7\) are roots of \(P(x)-a,\) write \(P(x)-a=(x-1)(x-3)\) \(\cdot(x-5)(x-7)Q(x)\) with \(Q\) having integer coefficients.

Evaluating at \(x=2, 4, 6, 8\) (where \(P=-a\)) gives \[ \begin{aligned} -2a &=-15\,Q(2) \\ &=9\,Q(4) \\ &=-15\,Q(6) \\ &=105\,Q(8). \end{aligned} \]

So \(15, 9,\) and \(105\) all divide \(2a,\) hence \(\operatorname{lcm}(15,9,105)=315\) divides \(2a.\) Since \(315\) is odd, \(a\) is divisible by \(315,\) so \(a\ge315.\)

To attain the bound, let \[ \begin{aligned} F(x)&=(x-1)(x-3) \\ &\quad\cdot(x-5)(x-7), \\ Q(x)&=42+(x-2)(x-6) \\ &\quad\cdot(60-8x), \\ P(x)&=315+F(x)Q(x). \end{aligned} \] This integer polynomial equals \(315\) at \(1,3,5,7.\) At \(2,4,\) the pairs \((F(x),Q(x))\) are \((-15,42),(9,-70),\) and at \(6,8\) they are \((-15,42),(105,-6).\) Thus \(F(x)Q(x)=-630\) each time and \(P(x)=-315.\) Hence the bound is attainable.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Evaluate at \(x=2,4,6,8\) to force \(2a\) to be divisible by \(\operatorname{lcm}(15,9,105)\)
